2. The High Court Division, by judgment and order dated 31-7-2011, confirmed the judgment and order of conviction dated 12-10-2006 passed by the learned Judge of the Durto Bichar Tribunal No.1, Dhaka(hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal)in Durto Bichar Tribunal Case No.7 of 2003 [arising out of GR Case No.3064 of 2002 (South) and Dhanmondi PS Case No. 62 (10) 02 dated 26-10-2002] of both the appellants Zalal alias Zillu and Maksudur Rahman Biplab under section 302/120B read with section 34 of the Penal Code; 1860. However, the High Court Division confirmed the sentence of death to appellant Zalal alias Zillu but modified the sentence of death of Maksudur Rahman Biplab by commuting the sentence of death to imprisonment for life. 

 7. Thus, my decision is that the order of conviction of appellant Zalal alias Zillu for the charges under sections 302/120B read with section 34 of the Penal Code, 1860 is affirmed. But his sentence of death be commuted to a sentence of imprisonment for life with the condition that he shall not be released before completing an actual term of 30 years imprisonment including the period already undergone by him with a fine of Taka 10,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a further period of I(one) year. 

 16. The Tribunal, upon considering the evidence adduced by the prosecution and other materials on record by its judgment and order dated 12-10-2006 convicted the appellants- Maksudur Rahman Biplob and Zalal alias Zillu under sections 302/120B/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced them to death. The Tribunal also convicted accused Porosh under sections 302/120B/34 of the Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced him to imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 50,000, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more. 

 18. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with .the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 12-10-2006 passed by the Tribunal the condemned prisoners preferred the above mentioned Criminal Appeals and Jail Appeals before the High Court Division. The High Court Division, upon hearing both the parties, rejected the death reference and dismissed the criminal appeal with jail appeal in respect of the Appellant-Maksudur Rahman Biplob and convicted the said appellant under sections 302/120B/34 of the Penal Code, 1860 modifying the sentence to imprisonment for life from death and accepted the. Death Reference No.103 of 2006 and dismissed the Criminal Appeal with Jail Appeal in respect of the. Appellant-Zalal alais Zillu by its judgment and order dated 31-7-2011 and thereby affirmed the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 12-10-2006 passed by the Tribunal. 

 22. Mr Biswajit Debnath, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent in both the Criminal Appeals made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that Tanvir Sharif Apan (shortly, Apan) and S. H. Sabbir Rahman Shantonu (in short Shantonu) were students of class VII in Dhanmondi Government Laboratory High School, Dhaka. The deceased Mr Swapan Goswami was a teacher of that school. However, when Shantonu and Apon participated in the class of VIII Goswami took them down to class seven as they failed in final examination of class VII. On the other hand, when Apon's mother met with Goswami, he insulted her. As a result, Apon and. Shantonu became furious on Goswami. They decided to engage Zalal, Biplab, Parash and others to kill him in exchange of Taka 1,00,000 (one lac). Shantonu gave a pistol owned by his father. On 24-10-2002, they made a conspiracy and chalked out a plan to kill Goswami. Accordingly, they visited the house of Goswami as students on the pretext of having tuition to him. However, they were not successful. On 25-10-2002 at 9-00 am they again made an attempt hatching a plan to commit dacoity at Swapan Goswami's house and kill him. Accordingly, on that day at 10-00 am they went to his house but unsuccessfully returned. He forcefully further submits that on the day of occurrence at about 9-15 am Zalal, Biplab and Refat again went to the place of occurrence to kill him. When Swapan Goswami came out of his house, they followed him. Goswami on his way to school stopped at Sikder Store to purchase cigarettes from the employee namely Monzu of the said store. At that time Zalal shot him at the head from behind. Goswami fell down, Zalal shot him twice more. Biplab then by a pistol shot him too. He submits that on 29-10-2002, 2nd Investigating Officer arrested the accused Refat Akond who made confessional statement on 30-10-2002. The confessional statement of Refat became the basis of the prosecution case. The Investigating Officer arrested other accused persons namely, Zalal, Shantonu and Apon. They also made confessional statements before the Magistrate confessing the guilt. In addition to the said accused persons' confessional statements, some witnesses also made statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Magistrate. The learned Deputy Attorney-General very strongly made submission against the two convict appellants Zalal alias Zillu and Maksudur Rahman Biplab. He submits that Zalal alias Zillu gave confessional statement before the Metropolitan Magistrate specifically admitting the conspiracy of killing and shooting Swapan Goswami. He also refers the testimony of PW 3- Mohammed Manzu, who is the eye witness, PW 4-Md Shamsul Islam, PW 5 Refat Akond who is the eye witness and approver in the case as per order of the Court. He next submits that the evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5 clearly depicted that confessional statement of the convict appellant Zalal alias Zillu is true and voluntary. Moreover, all the ocular evidence and confessional statement of convict appellant are similar and supportive. Therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is well founded. He next submits that convict-appellant Maksudur Rahman Biplab also stands on the same footing in the instant case. He refers the testimonies of the PWs 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 and argued that the said PWs in a voice supported the shooting by the convict-appellant Maksudur Rahman Biplab to deceased Showpan Goswami. He tries to refute the legal arguments advanced by the learned Advocate for the convict-appellant Biplab saying that non-examination of the approver by the Pardoning Court as witness is a technical ground for which the position of the approver cannot be changed. He also submits that the approver Refat Aknond also made confessional statement before the Metropolitan Magistrate. The testimony of the PW 5 Refat Akon as an approver shows that he has given the full and true discloser of the facts. Therefore, treating him as an approver is lawful. In support of his arguments he has relied upon the decisions reported in 7 DLR (FC) 178, 8 BLC 275, 4 DLR 247, (2010) 10 SCC 179.
